memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Reason for visit: evaluation of abnormal liver enzymes and fatigue.
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: The patient reports mild right upper quadrant discomfort and intermittent tiredness for 2 months.
EXAMINATION: BP 118/76 mmHg, weight 62 kg, height 158 cm, BMI 24.8 (overweight). Abdomen soft, no hepatomegaly.
IMPRESSION: Likely non‑alcoholic fatty liver disease and vitamin D deficiency.
ARRANGEMENTS: Advised balanced diet, reduced refined sugars, 150 min/week brisk walking. Started silymarin 140 mg TDS, rosuvastatin 5 mg OD, cholecalciferol 60 000 IU once weekly for 8 weeks then 1000 IU OD. Return if: jaundice, worsening abdominal pain, fever >39 °C, dark urine, or unexplained weight loss.

memories.text: ALT 48 U/L (7‑35), AST 42 U/L (8‑33), ALP 84 U/L (40‑129), GGT 38 U/L (9‑48). Total bilirubin 0.9 mg/dL (0.2‑1.2). Albumin 4.2 g/dL (3.5‑5.0). Platelets 210 ×10⁹/L (150‑400). Lipid profile: TC 210 mg/dL (<200), LDL 130 mg/dL (<100), HDL 48 mg/dL (>40), TG 160 mg/dL (<150). Serum 25‑OH vitamin D 14 ng/mL (30‑100). Calcium 9.2 mg/dL (8.5‑10.5), phosphate 3.4 mg/dL (2.5‑4.5).

memories.author: patient
memories.text: I have been feeling a bit more energetic after starting the medicines, but I still notice a mild heaviness under my right rib cage after meals. My appetite is okay and I have been trying to walk around the neighbourhood for about 20 minutes most days.

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Reason for visit: 6‑week follow‑up on NAFLD and vitamin D repletion.
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Patient reports reduced right upper quadrant discomfort and improved energy.
EXAMINATION: BP 120/78 mmHg, weight 61.5 kg, BMI 24.6 (overweight). Abdomen soft, no tenderness.
IMPRESSION: Improving liver enzymes; vitamin D still low, needs maintenance.
ARRANGEMENTS: Continue silymarin and rosuvastatin. Change vitamin D to cholecalciferol 1000 IU OD. Encourage Mediterranean‑style diet, limit fried foods, aim for 30 min walk daily. Return if: worsening abdominal pain, jaundice, fever >39 °C, sudden weight gain, or shortness of breath.

memories.author: D03
memories.text: Abdominal ultrasound: Liver shows diffuse increased echogenicity consistent with mild hepatic steatosis. Portal vein normal, no focal lesions. Gallbladder wall normal, no stones. No ascites. Spleen size normal. Impression: Mild NAFLD, no evidence of fibrosis or cirrhosis.

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Reason for visit: Review of ultrasound results and ongoing NAFLD management.
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Patient says discomfort has resolved; she feels well.
EXAMINATION: BP 119/77 mmHg, weight 61 kg, BMI 24.4 (overweight). Abdomen soft, no hepatomegaly.
IMPRESSION: Ultrasound confirms mild steatosis, labs improving. Vitamin D still suboptimal.
ARRANGEMENTS: Continue current meds. Advise weight reduction target 5‑7 % over 3 months, increase aerobic activity to 150 min/week, avoid alcohol. Offered influenza vaccine (given today, 01‑Sep‑2025). Return if: jaundice, worsening abdominal pain, fever >39 °C, dark urine, or unexplained fatigue.

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Reason for visit: Routine follow‑up after 3 months of NAFLD therapy.
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Patient reports no abdominal discomfort, good energy levels.
EXAMINATION: BP 118/76 mmHg, weight 60.5 kg, BMI 24.2 (overweight). Abdomen soft.
IMPRESSION: Labs show continued improvement; vitamin D now sufficient.
ARRANGEMENTS: Continue silymarin and rosuvastatin. Vitamin D cholecalciferol 1000 IU OD to maintain levels. Reinforce diet low in refined carbs, regular exercise 30 min daily. Influenza vaccine already given this season. Return if: jaundice, worsening abdominal pain, fever >39 °C, unexplained weight loss, or severe fatigue.

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Reason for visit: Annual review of NAFLD and vitamin D status.
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Patient feels well, no symptoms.
EXAMINATION: BP 119/77 mmHg, weight 60 kg, BMI 24.0 (overweight). Abdomen soft, no hepatomegaly.
IMPRESSION: Stable mild steatosis on prior ultrasound, labs within normal ranges, vitamin D adequate.
ARRANGEMENTS: Continue silymarin 140 mg TDS and rosuvastatin 5 mg OD. Vitamin D cholecalciferol 1000 IU OD maintenance. Advise maintain weight, Mediterranean diet, 150 min/week activity. Influenza vaccine offered for upcoming season (to be given Oct‑Nov). Return if: jaundice, worsening abdominal pain, fever >39 °C, dark urine, or unexplained fatigue.
